phases.message: I asked the state's Erasepoint to make data brokers delete me back in January, and I'm still on people-search sites. Start with my Privacy folder: what has each broker told me?
This is my request on Erasepoint. Check each broker's status, fix anything my request is missing, and complain about any broker that's ignoring the law.
Now Findwho. Find what's still up about me and get my listings removed. Leave my family and anyone who just shares my name alone.
And Lookabout. Same here, then tell me what you did and when I should check again.

rules.text: Topics: request, brokers, statuses, agents, complaints. One request on Erasepoint directs every registered data broker to delete your personal information (Civil Code §1798.99.86).

Brokers match your request only against the identifiers on it. Add every name, email, phone and address you have used, including a former name; a broker cannot find a record under a name you did not give.

From 2026-08-01 each broker retrieves requests at least every 45 days, must process each request and report its status within 45 days of retrieving it, and must delete matching information it collects later on the same 45-day cycle.

Record deleted; opted out of sale (the broker could not verify the request, so the law directs it to stop selling and sharing your information rather than delete it); exempt (the information falls under an exemption, such as consumer report data under the federal FCRA); not found. You may still send a deletion request to a broker directly under the CCPA (Civil Code §1798.105).
You may act only for yourself. Someone acting for another adult needs that person's signed permission as an authorized agent; a parent cannot act for an adult child.

Complain when a broker has not reported a status within 45 days of retrieving your request, or keeps your information after reporting it deleted beyond its next 45-day cycle. A lawful status (opted out when unverified, exempt, not found) is not a violation.
